findings.text: Updates access state for a huge mapping. For a non contiguous entry it delegates to a generic any size helper. For a contiguous run it first tests whether write dirty or young state differs across the run; if unchanged it reports no update, otherwise it clears the whole run with flush, carries forward dirty and young from the cleared value into the new entry, installs the entry across the run, and reports a change. Present state of proposed and cleared entries is checked with debug warnings.

Covers write protection and clearing plus protection change bracketing for huge entries. Write protection uses a generic helper for non contiguous entries and otherwise clears with flush, applies write protection, then reinstalls over the run. Clearing with flush derives contiguous count and base size from the owning area huge state and returns the flushed entry. Modification start selects a flush variant for an executable user entry under an erratum capability and otherwise uses a get and clear form; commit reinstalls the new entry for the same huge size. Size validation delegates to a shared huge size predicate.

Boot time registration of supported huge states. Enforces a build time minimum on the maximum huge state count, then conditionally registers a largest block level when section support is present, followed by three further levels covering contiguous middle, middle and contiguous leaf sizes. Runs once during initialization and reports success.

A contiguous run is considered changed when the write permission of the proposed entry differs from the current first entry, or when any entry in the run differs in dirty or young state from the proposal. The scan covers the full run length supplied by the caller and returns a boolean style indicator.

When a specific ARM erratum capability is present, changing protections on a user executable huge entry must use a break before make flush path rather than plain get and clear. The start helper checks the capability and the executable state of the current entry to select the safe path; mishandling would violate the erratum requirement for executable to non executable transitions.

Early memory setup entry points. One resolves the architectural zero page from a well known empty symbol. Another prepares bounce buffering and validates build configuration. A third marks the page allocator available and updates bounce attributes. A fourth releases the init image region through the linear alias, checks page alignment of its bounds, frees it as unused kernel memory, then unmaps the virtual range while leaving the area reserved against module reuse.

Pre initialization sizes the bounce buffer when all memory sits below the DMA limit, scaling with total physical memory and capping at a default, then initializes bounce handling verbosely. It enforces build time consistency of compat task size against map window and of derived versus configured page table levels. On very small systems with large base pages it forces memory overcommit to always.

Init memory release operates on the linear alias of the init bounds, warns on misalignment, frees with a poison pattern and a descriptive tag, then removes the virtual mapping without freeing the virtual area, preventing later reuse for modules that would confuse symbol resolution.

Zone limit setup derives a DMA32 top from a 32 bit mask and programs per zone upper page frame numbers from DMA, DMA32 and total limits under configuration guards. Early boot parameter parsing accepts a memory size string, masks to page granularity, records it as a global limit and logs the capped megabytes; a missing string reports failure.

Platform and range checks. Confidential compute attributes for memory encryption report true only in realm or protected guest states. Physical range validation requires coverage by mapped memory without nomap exclusion for the whole extent, and mmap physical validation requires the addressed extent to fit within the physical mask. Access protection for physical memory selects non cached for non mappable frames, write combining when opened synchronous, otherwise leaves caller protection. RAM remap permission mirrors whether the starting frame belongs to mappable memory.

Memstart granularity alternatives. Shift is defined from a pud, contiguous middle or middle level shift depending on configuration. Alignment is defined either from section size bits or from the selected shift. Together they constrain the physical memory start granularity.

Kernel mapping restriction flags. Bit zero forbids block mappings, bit one forbids contiguous mappings, bit two forbids executable mappings under an assumption about a hardware feature. Stored as small integer bit masks.
Kasan shadow alignment is defined as either a fourth level or third level table size depending on configuration. The kasan log prefix formats messages with a fixed subsystem tag.

Boot mode table holds two ordered entries for EL2 then EL1. Read only after init globals include a signed physical start defaulting to negative one, a DMA physical limit, a kernel image virtual offset, a read only data writability flag defaulting true, and module region bases defaulting to zero.

Two global synchronization objects guard early page table work. A spin lock protects the top level kernel directory updates. A mutex serializes fixed mapping updates. Both are statically initialized and have file scope.

A mutex serializes page table splitting to leaf entries. A file scope boolean records whether the linear map conversion requires a specific break before make level. The flag is consulted during linear map maintenance.

Early kasan setup validates shadow geometry at build time, installs a temporary next level table when the shadow start shares a top level entry with the linear region to avoid corruption of shared zero shadow tables, then populates shadow coverage for the whole shadow interval. A second helper populates shadow only for vmalloc or module addresses, aligning the derived shadow extent to page boundaries.

Build time checks require the shadow offset to match shadow end minus the scaled address space size and require alignment of minimum and current shadow starts and shadow end to the configured shadow alignment. Misaligned start handling uses a static zero initialized leaf table in a dedicated page table section and points the top entry at it as a table descriptor.

Optional memory encryption hooks. Both set encrypted and set decrypted are no ops returning success when no operations vector is installed, warn and return success on misaligned addresses, otherwise delegate to the installed vector encrypt or decrypt operation for the requested page count.

A sixteen entry read only after init table maps combinations of none read write exec and shared into initial page protections, with read only defaults for private writes, execute variants mapping to read execute, and shared writes mapping to shared variants. Boot adjustment upgrades execute only entries when enhanced privilege access never is present, and on a large address extension strips the shared attribute from every entry and from the shadow stack protection.

Derives page protection from virtual memory flags by table lookup on read write exec shared, with a fast path for shadow stack that honours accessless mappings as none and otherwise uses a dedicated shadow stack value. Branch target identification adds a guard bit, memory tagging selects a tagged normal type when requested, and permission overlay index bits are added when supported.

Linear map conversion to leaf entries has distinct boot and secondary roles. The boot processor waits until a counter flag shows all online processors parked, splits the linear interval excluding the kernel alias in two ranges with atomic allocation, flushes the kernel translation cache for the whole interval, then clears the flag with an ordered store. Secondaries install the identity map, invoke a physical wait routine until the boot processor finishes, then uninstall the identity map and continue.

A page table walk splits large entries down to leaves. The pud callback splits leaf puds, the pmd callback first splits contiguous middle entries then leaf pmds and skips per leaf revisits, the pte callback splits contiguous leaf runs. The range helper brackets the lockless walk with lazy mmu mode enable and disable and forwards an allocation context.

Executable memory setup computes module region placement then publishes range descriptors. Without address randomization it anchors direct and PLT regions below the kernel end when the kernel is small enough; with randomization it optionally randomizes a small direct window and always randomizes a large PLT window around the kernel image, logging usable page counts. The published info prefers the direct window with PLT fallback when present, otherwise uses PLT only, and assigns vmalloc ranges to probes and BPF with distinct protections.

Randomized region placement returns zero meaning use default when the existing kernel extent already fits inside the requested window. Otherwise it computes the maximum page offset that still encloses the kernel extent, draws an inclusive uniform random offset within that bound, and returns a start below the kernel start by that many pages.

Hibernate notification toggles validity of the linear alias covering post init data up to the end of writable data. Prepare marks it valid, post restore marks it invalid; other notification modes are ignored. The helper derives page count from the distance between init end and data end through the linear alias.

Early page table allocation reserves a page from the physical allocator and panics on failure. Two wrappers allocate init and special top level tables for the kernel with kernel page table allocation flags, one for a given level via an init variant and one without an owning address space.

Fatal and warning paths. Early page allocation and linear map splitting panic with descriptive messages on failure. Init bounds misalignment warns. Huge access helpers warn when present expectations are violated. Module region geometry and huge state count plus page table level consistency are enforced at build time; violation prevents boot image construction.

Observed executable memory descriptor layout as used by setup. It contains an array of ranges indexed by usage kind covering default, probes and BPF, each with numeric start and end, protection value and alignment, with the default range additionally carrying fallback start and end for PLT reach. No full type definition appears in the fragments; only this usage shape is visible.

Remaining file scope state. A hook pointer customizes IO remap protections. A constant operations pointer for memory encryption defaults to absent. A boolean early KFENCE flag defaults from configuration. A 64 bit flag coordinates secondary parking for KPTI work. Read only after init qualifiers protect start, limit, offset and base values after boot.
